title: Finding the vector sum of two forces
canonical_question: How do you find the vector sum of two forces acting at an angle?
summary: Two forces pulling in different directions do not combine to their arithmetic total, because direction matters as much as size.
A reliable method is to break each force into horizontal and vertical parts, add the horizontal parts and the vertical parts separately, then recombine.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Why plain addition fails
sections.body_md: Two forces pulling in different directions do not combine to their arithmetic total, because direction matters as much as size. The correct combination is the vector sum: lay the arrows head to tail and read off the single arrow that closes the path. That resulting arrow is what actually acts on the body.

sections.heading: Doing it with components
sections.body_md: A reliable method is to break each force into horizontal and vertical parts, add the horizontal parts and the vertical parts separately, then recombine. The recombined horizontal and vertical totals give the size and direction of the vector sum. Components turn a geometry problem into simple arithmetic.

key_points: Direction matters, so forces need vector addition.
Adding components is the reliable numerical method.
core.bridge_to_parent: It expands the vector meaning of net force from the objective.
